n9-licao-plantao.enunciado:
In this level, every mission is an incident: the cluster arrives broken, a resident tells you what they saw, and you investigate and fix it. The applied manifests are in the editor (change them and click Apply) and the terminal is yours.

The playbook

  1. kubectl get pods (with -o wide and -A): the STATUS already points the way.
  2. kubectl describe pod NAME: the Events at the end tell you what Kubernetes tried and why it failed. Give the full name: with several pods (no name, or just the start of it), describe hides the Events. To see all of them at once, kubectl get events.
  3. kubectl logs NAME (and --previous, if it restarted): what the program itself said.
  4. kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp: the namespace’s logbook.
  5. kubectl exec: go inside and test from there (wget, nslookup, cat).

From symptom to cause

SymptomWhere to lookCommon causes
Pendingdescribe pod (FailedScheduling)not enough CPU/memory, taint, nodeSelector, PVC, quota
ImagePullBackOffdescribe podwrong name or tag, private registry
CrashLoopBackOfflogs --previousmissing env or file, bug, OOMKilled
CreateContainerConfigErrordescribe podmissing ConfigMap/Secret, runAsNonRoot
Running, 0/1 readydescribe pod (Unhealthy)wrong readinessProbe
Service doesn’t answerget endpoints, describe svcselector, targetPort, nobody ready, NetworkPolicy
Forbiddenauth can-i --asverb or resource missing from the Role

A golden rule: change one thing at a time and check again. And read the whole error message: it almost always tells you exactly what’s missing.
n9-licao-plantao.vidaReal: The on-call building manager doesn’t go around replacing everything: they listen to the resident, check the logbook, go into the apartment, and only then call the right electrician.
n9-licao-plantao.limite: In the condo, the building manager sees the damage with their own eyes. In the cluster, you only see what the commands show you: learn to ask.

n9-imagem-errada.enunciado:
The new storefront still hasn’t opened. The guy said all he had to do was put up nginx and leave.

Marta, who runs the clothing store in unit 101

Find out why the vitrine (storefront) pods won’t come up, and fix it.
n9-imagem-errada.dica: kubectl describe pod NAME (Events: Failed to pull image). Check how the image name is spelled.
n9-imagem-errada.vidaReal: The prefab part never arrived: the model was misspelled on the order.
n9-imagem-errada.limite: The kubelet retries on its own, slower each time: fixing the name solves it without deleting anything.

n9-sem-senha.enunciado:
The database has been restarting nonstop since the move. The password is in the usual envelope, I swear.

Jorge, from finance

The banco (database) Secret (key senha) already exists. Find out what the database asks for and hand it the password, read from the Secret.
n9-sem-senha.dica: kubectl logs deploy/banco --previous asks for POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Use env with valueFrom.secretKeyRef.
n9-sem-senha.vidaReal: The database’s doorman won’t open up without the password, and nobody ever handed him the envelope.
n9-sem-senha.limite: The envelope (Secret) was there all along: storing it isn’t enough, you have to tell the pod to read it.

msgs.1: the password comes from the banco Secret

n9-sem-espaco.enunciado:
I asked for the monthly report at eight. It’s been “waiting” ever since. Waiting for what?

Zélia, from accounting

The relatorio (report) pod is Pending. Find out why and change the request to something reasonable (half a CPU core is enough).
n9-sem-espaco.dica: kubectl describe pod NAME (0/3 nodes are available: ... Insufficient cpu). Each node has 2 CPUs.
n9-sem-espaco.vidaReal: Someone asked for an apartment with the power of three buildings: no building in the condo has that much electricity.
n9-sem-espaco.limite: The request is what gets reserved, not what gets used: asking for too much leaves the pod with nowhere to go, even with idle nodes.

n9-manutencao-esquecida.enunciado:
Yesterday there was maintenance in both buildings. Today the new shop can’t move in anywhere.

Kleber, the caretaker

The loja (shop) pods are Pending. Find out what the maintenance left behind and remove it.
n9-manutencao-esquecida.dica: kubectl describe node (the Taints line) and kubectl taint nodes NODE key-.
n9-manutencao-esquecida.vidaReal: Someone forgot the “under renovation” sign hanging on the doors of both buildings.
n9-manutencao-esquecida.limite: Taking down the sign only lets the next ones in: whoever was turned away waits for the scheduler’s next attempt.

msgs.1: node-1 no longer has the sign
msgs.2: node-2 no longer has the sign

n9-disco-que-nao-vem.titulo: The storage unit that was never delivered
n9-disco-que-nao-vem.enunciado:
I rented a storage unit for the gallery’s photos, and the gallery never even opened. They said the unit was the “fast” kind.

Lauro, the photographer

The galeria (gallery) is waiting for the fotos disk, which never becomes ready. Find out why and use the disk class that exists in the cluster.
n9-disco-que-nao-vem.dica: kubectl describe pvc fotos and kubectl get storageclass. Since the PVC can’t change, kubectl delete -f . and then kubectl apply -f .
n9-disco-que-nao-vem.vidaReal: They asked for a “climate-controlled” storage unit, and the condo only has regular ones: the request sits in the drawer forever.
n9-disco-que-nao-vem.limite: A storage unit request (PVC) can’t be edited once it’s made: to change the class, you delete it and ask again.

n9-ramal-mudo.enunciado:
The shop’s clerks are all there, I saw them. But whoever calls the “loja” extension doesn’t reach anyone.

Lúcia, from customer service

The shop’s pods are ready, but the loja Service doesn’t deliver to them. Fix the Service.
n9-ramal-mudo.dica: kubectl get endpoints loja (empty) and compare the Service’s selector with the pods’ labels (--show-labels).
n9-ramal-mudo.vidaReal: The extension is registered to the “lojas” team, and the team is called “loja”.
n9-ramal-mudo.limite: The Service doesn’t warn you that its selector matches nobody: it just keeps an empty list of clerks.

n9-porta-errada.enunciado:
Now the extension at least rings, but it hangs up right away: “connection refused”.

Lúcia, from customer service

The loja Service has the 3 pods behind it, but nobody answers. Find out which port the shop listens on and fix the Service.
n9-porta-errada.dica: kubectl describe svc loja (TargetPort) and the pods’ containerPort. The shop listens on 8080.
n9-porta-errada.vidaReal: The extension rings the phone on the next desk: the clerks are in the apartment, but in the other room.
n9-porta-errada.limite: The Service checks who’s ready, not which port the program listens on: the list is full and the call drops.

n9-nunca-pronto.enunciado:
The shop’s three clerks arrived early and they’re inside. But I can’t send customers to someone who doesn’t say they’re ready.

Apolinário, the doorman

The loja pods run, but stay at 0/1 and the Service has nobody. Fix the readinessProbe.
n9-nunca-pronto.dica: kubectl describe pod NAME (Events: Unhealthy, Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404). The shop answers on /healthz.
n9-nunca-pronto.vidaReal: The building manager asks “can you take visitors?” at the wrong door: nobody answers, and he marks it as closed.
n9-nunca-pronto.limite: Readiness doesn’t restart anyone: the pod keeps running forever, it just doesn’t get any customers.

n9-disjuntor.titulo: The circuit breaker that keeps tripping
n9-disjuntor.enunciado:
The report starts, the lights flicker and it’s gone. It starts again, flicker, gone.

Zélia, from accounting

The relatorio loads the whole spreadsheet into memory (about 300Mi). Find out why it crashes and give it a limit that fits (512Mi).
n9-disjuntor.dica: kubectl describe pod NAME (Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled). Change limits.memory.
n9-disjuntor.vidaReal: The apartment’s circuit breaker is rated 128, and the accounting machine draws 300 when it turns on.
n9-disjuntor.limite: Raising the limit solves it when the program really needs that much. If it leaks memory, it only delays the next crash.

n9-quadro-sem-aviso.enunciado:
The new storefront was supposed to be blue. Not blue, not anything: it won’t even open.

Marta, who runs the clothing store in unit 101

The vitrine pods can’t create their container. Find out what’s missing and create it, with COR=azul.
n9-quadro-sem-aviso.dica: kubectl describe pod NAME (configmap "vitrine-config" not found). kubectl create configmap vitrine-config --from-literal=COR=azul
n9-quadro-sem-aviso.vidaReal: The storefront reads its color from the bulletin board, and the board was never put up.
n9-quadro-sem-aviso.limite: As soon as the ConfigMap shows up, the kubelet tries again and the storefront comes up: no need to restart anything.

n9-catraca-esquecida.enunciado:
Since the security audit, the storefront can’t talk to the shop anymore. Only the admin folks get through.

Rafa, from the storefront

The protege-loja NetworkPolicy only lets app=admin pods into the shop. Let the vitrine in too, without opening it to everyone.
n9-catraca-esquecida.dica: kubectl get netpol and kubectl describe netpol protege-loja. Add a podSelector app: vitrine to the from.
n9-catraca-esquecida.vidaReal: The new turnstile only recognizes the admin badge: the storefront gets stopped at the door.
n9-catraca-esquecida.limite: Deleting the turnstile also “solves” it, and opens the shop to anyone (including the nosy curioso pod).

msgs.1: the curioso pod is still blocked

n9-sem-cracha.enunciado:
The pipeline creates Deployments in the shop just fine, but when it tries to update one, it gets this: deployments.apps "loja" is forbidden: User "carla" cannot patch resource "deployments" in API group "apps" in the namespace "loja".

Carla, from the deploy pipeline (CI)

Give the deploy-ci Role what’s missing for carla to update Deployments (update and patch), without giving her the power to delete.
n9-sem-cracha.dica: kubectl auth can-i patch deployments --as=carla -n loja. Add update and patch to the verbs.
n9-sem-cracha.vidaReal: The badge opens the door to bring in new furniture, but not to replace what’s already there.
n9-sem-cracha.limite: kubectl apply uses patch; kubectl replace uses update. So the pipeline doesn’t depend on which one, give it both.

n9-endereco-errado.titulo: The stockroom in the other block
n9-endereco-errado.enunciado:
The storefront moved to the shop’s block and now says “stockroom down” all the time. The stockroom is working, I called them.

Rafa, from the storefront

The vitrine (namespace loja) calls the stockroom’s api at the address in the API_URL variable. But the api lives in the estoque namespace. Fix the address.
n9-endereco-errado.dica: kubectl logs -n loja deploy/vitrine (wget: bad address). The address is http://api.estoque.
n9-endereco-errado.vidaReal: They dialed the “api” extension in their own block; the api is in another block, and the short address doesn’t reach it.
n9-endereco-errado.limite: The short name only works within the same namespace: from another one, it’s name.namespace (or the full name, name.namespace.svc.cluster.local).

msgs.1: API_URL points to the estoque namespace

n9-rollout-travado.titulo: The renovation that won’t move forward
n9-rollout-travado.enunciado:
They moved the shop to the new version this morning. The “rollout status” still says it’s waiting. At least the old shop is still serving customers.

Jorge, from finance

The loja update is stuck. Find out why and take the shop back to a version that exists (the previous one will do).
n9-rollout-travado.dica: kubectl rollout status deployment/loja, kubectl get pods (ErrImagePull on the new tag). kubectl rollout undo deployment/loja
n9-rollout-travado.vidaReal: The step-by-step renovation stopped at the first apartment: the new material never arrived, and the old ones are still standing.
n9-rollout-travado.limite: The Deployment doesn’t give up on its own: after the deadline (progressDeadlineSeconds), it just marks “ProgressDeadlineExceeded” and waits for someone to decide.

n9-job-que-falha.enunciado:
The database migration ran overnight and says “failed”. It tried three times and gave up.

Jorge, from finance

Find out why the migracao (migration) Job fails, fix it and run it again.
n9-job-que-falha.dica: kubectl logs job/migracao (sh: slep: not found). Then: kubectl delete job migracao and kubectl apply -f .
n9-job-que-falha.vidaReal: The bricklayer tried three times to follow the misspelled instruction (“slep” instead of “sleep”) and went home.
n9-job-que-falha.limite: A Job’s pod template can’t be edited after it’s created: to run it again with the fix, you delete the Job and create another one.

n9-limpeza-suspensa.titulo: The garbage pickup that never came
n9-limpeza-suspensa.enunciado:
The garbage pickup was supposed to come every minute. It hasn’t come once this week.

Kleber, the caretaker

The limpeza (cleanup) CronJob never created a Job. Find out why and bring the pickup back.
n9-limpeza-suspensa.dica: kubectl get cronjob limpeza (the SUSPEND column). Change suspend to false and apply.
n9-limpeza-suspensa.vidaReal: Someone hung a “pickup suspended” sign during last week’s renovation and nobody took it down.
n9-limpeza-suspensa.limite: When it comes back, the pickup doesn’t make up for the times it missed: it carries on from the next scheduled time.

n9-fila-presa.titulo: The queue stuck in the building without power
n9-fila-presa.enunciado:
node-2 lost power and the order queue stopped. The shop came back in another building, but the queue never does.

Lúcia, from customer service

The fila (queue) is a StatefulSet with one replica, and the pod fila-0 got stuck Terminating on node-2, which isn’t coming back today. Bring the queue back in another building.
n9-fila-presa.dica: kubectl get pods -o wide and kubectl get nodes. The StatefulSet waits for fila-0 to be gone for good: kubectl delete pod fila-0 --force --grace-period=0
n9-fila-presa.vidaReal: Apartment 0 of the queue has an owner and a number: until the management office is sure the old one has left, it won’t give that number to anyone else.
n9-fila-presa.limite: Forcing it out means stating “the old one really is dead”. If the building comes back and the old one is still alive, there would be two fila-0s.

n9-balcao-errado.titulo: The front desk sends people to the wrong room
n9-balcao-errado.enunciado:
People who come through the front gate looking for loja.local get “Service Unavailable”. The shop is open, I saw it.

Apolinário, the doorman

The loja Ingress sends loja.local to a Service that doesn’t exist. Fix it.
n9-balcao-errado.dica: kubectl describe ingress loja (Backends) and kubectl get svc.
n9-balcao-errado.vidaReal: The information desk sends customers to the “lojas” room, and the room is called “loja”.
n9-balcao-errado.limite: The Ingress doesn’t check whether the Service exists when it’s created: the error only shows up when someone arrives.

n9-cota-estourada.titulo: We asked for six, we got four
n9-cota-estourada.enunciado:
For the sale, I asked for six clerks. Four showed up. The general manager already approved a quota of ten.

Cida, the sales manager

The loja in the vendas (sales) namespace has 6 replicas and only 4 pods. Find out what’s holding it back and apply the approved quota: 10 pods.
n9-cota-estourada.dica: kubectl describe rs -n vendas (exceeded quota) and kubectl describe quota -n vendas. Change hard.pods to "10".
n9-cota-estourada.vidaReal: The company can only have four apartments in the condo: the lease for the other two gets turned down at the front gate.
n9-cota-estourada.limite: The quota refuses at creation time, quietly: the Deployment shows 4/6, and the reason only shows up in the ReplicaSet’s events.

n9-pintura-sem-fim.titulo: The paint job that never ends
n9-pintura-sem-fim.enunciado:
The new dashboard has been “Init:0/1” since yesterday. The painting crew showed up and is just standing at the door.

Lauro, the photographer

The init container of the painel (dashboard) waits for the database by name before letting the dashboard start. Find out what it’s waiting for, what the database is really called (kubectl get svc), and fix it.
n9-pintura-sem-fim.dica: kubectl logs deploy/painel -c espera-o-banco (it prints: esperando o banco). The Service is called db: replace banco with db in the name the init container looks for.
n9-pintura-sem-fim.vidaReal: The painting crew is waiting for the resident “banco” to arrive, and the resident is called “db”: they’ll wait forever.
n9-pintura-sem-fim.limite: An init container has no deadline: without a timeout in the script, it waits indefinitely, with no error at all.
